requirements.topic: Definition — Flight Instructor (Instructor Pilot)
requirements.requirement: A Flight Instructor (Instructor Pilot) is a flyer holding a Flight Instructor Rating on the aircraft type, who may occupy any crew position according to training requirements. Additionally, a radionavigator graduate of the SIR who is available on type may be appointed by DAE as a 'Military Instructor' for air training.

Ιπτάμενος, κάτοχος Πτυχίου Εκπαιδευτή Πτήσεων στον τύπο Α/Φ, που καταλαμβάνει οποιαδήποτε θέση χειρισμού, ανάλογα με τις απαιτήσεις εκπαίδευσης. β. Ειδικότερα ο απόφοιτος της ΣΙΡ, ειδικότητας Ραδιοναυτίλου, ο οποίος είναι διαθέσιμος στον τύπο του Α/Φ, χρησιμοποιείται για την εκπαίδευση αέρος και έχει οριστεί από τη ΔΑΕ ως «Στρατιωτικός Εκπαιδευτής» στις πτήσεις.

requirements.topic: Definitions — Pilot in Command and Pilot in Control (co-pilot sorties)
requirements.requirement: In a co-pilot sortie the Pilot in Command is the most senior flyer available on type; if a Flight Instructor, he may occupy any seat. If the most senior is a trainee or not available in an event, the PIC (only during training or re-assignment) is the one available in the event. Between instructors of different states: PIC is the senior in rank; at equal rank, the holder of the greater formation-lead title; if both tie, the squadron CO ordering the flight designates the PIC. The Pilot in Control is the flyer who has control of the aircraft in a specific segment of the flight.

requirements.topic: Definition — Flight Simulator Instructor and Air Escort
requirements.requirement: A Flight Simulator Instructor is a flyer, graduate of the Ground Instructor School (SEE), trained and appointed to provide instruction in the simulator devices. An Air Escort (Synodos Aeros) is a flyer who flies to fulfil the training objectives of a student/trainee exercise in which he is available; he is a formation member employed according to the formation-lead title he holds.
requirements.verbatim: 5. Συνοδός Αέρος Ιπτάμενος που ίπταται για την εκπλήρωση των ΑΝΣΚ της άσκησης, σταδίου μαθητών ή εκπαιδευομένων, στην οποία είναι διαθέσιμος. Αποτελεί μέλος του σχηματισμού και χρησιμοποιείται ανάλογα με την αρχηγία που διαθέτει. 6. requirements.topic: Definition — Air Test Pilot (Dokimastis Aeros)
requirements.requirement: An Air Test Pilot is a flyer who has completed the prescribed training on the aircraft type and has been appointed to execute Functional Check Flights (FCF).
requirements.verbatim: 7. Δοκιμαστής Αέρος Ιπτάμενος που έχει ολοκληρώσει την προβλεπόμενη εκπαίδευση επί του τύπου του Α/Φ και έχει ορισθεί για την εκτέλεση Πτήσεων Δοκιμής (FCF).

requirements.topic: Definitions — Training Flight, Night Flight (75% rule), Maintenance Flight, FCF
requirements.requirement: A Training Flight is a flight flown to train or examine flying personnel, by a flyer holding a Flight Instructor Rating; during it the instructor may occupy any seat depending on the exercise or training stage. A NIGHT FLIGHT is a flight at least 75% of whose duration is flown at night (machine-usable threshold for schedulers). A Maintenance Flight is flown within the squadrons' maintenance programme to retain and progressively improve skills acquired and successfully evaluated in the training phases. A Test Flight (FCF) monitors, accepts, certifies and functionally checks an aircraft, system or carried load; details and FCF categories per KPA G-4/GEA.
requirements.verbatim: 8. Εκπαιδευτική Πτήση [...] Είναι η πτήση που εκτελείται με σκοπό την εκπαίδευση ή εξέταση του Ιπτάμενου προσωπικού, από Ιπτάμενο που κατέχει Πτυχίο Εκπαιδευτή Πτήσεων. Ο Εκπαιδευτής Πτήσεων, κατά την πτήση, δύναται να καταλαμβάνει οποιαδήποτε θέση, ανάλογα με την εκτελούμενη άσκηση ή το στάδιο εκπαίδευσης. 9. Λεπτομέρειες για τις Πτήσεις Δοκιμής καθώς και για τις κατηγορίες στις οποίες διακρίνονται περιγράφονται στον ΚΠΑ Γ-4/ΓΕΑ.

requirements.topic: Definitions — Flyer categories (student, trainee, posted, attached, flight surgeon)
requirements.requirement: Flyer categories: Student (Icarus cadet, SI-graduate 2Lt, foreign officer in a flight-training stage, or SMYA radionavigator student); Trainee (officer training at MEAE/SMET to become an instructor or to be assigned/re-assigned on type, including doctors under training); Posted flyer (instructor belonging to the squadron's strength); Attached flyer (instructor officer not on squadron strength, attached by GEA order only for type continuation or to assist the squadron's work); Flying Doctor (IIAI doctor who after training maintains currency in the rear seat). Attached flyers who belong to Plan IKAROS Phase A, attached GEA/DAE Air Evaluators, and instructors posted to SOT must maintain BMC (combat-ready level A); the Wing CO, Deputy CO, DEE, DPD and IKAROS Phases B and C maintain type availability only.

requirements.topic: Experience level — definition of EXPERIENCED instructor (thresholds)
requirements.requirement: An instructor is characterised EXPERIENCED if he meets any one of: (a) 600 hours on the squadron's type as instructor, with no prior fighter experience; (b) 1,000 hours total, of which 250 on the squadron's type as flight instructor; (c) 300 hours as pilot-in-command on fighters or other jet/turboprop trainer aircraft AND 250 hours on the squadron's type as instructor — if fewer than 300 fighter hours, the squadron-type hours increase by 2 for every 1 hour short of 300; (d) 150 hours on the squadron's type as instructor, when previously characterised experienced on fighters or experienced instructor on jet/turboprop aircraft. All other instructors are inexperienced (apeiroi) by implication.

requirements.topic: Instructors — general responsibility statement (Chapter 1)
requirements.requirement: Instructors must know the technique of executing and teaching the exercises and are responsible for providing complete training to students/trainees, aiming at high professional competence, cultivation of fighting spirit, and attainment-maintenance of the required high flying ability.

requirements.topic: Chain of training responsibilities (DAE / 120PEA / Squadron Commanders / Instructors)

requirements.topic: Daily flight programme — drafted by squadron, approved by Squadron Commander or Training Officer (AE)
requirements.requirement: Squadron training flights are flown per the Daily Flight Programme, which is drafted by the squadron and approved by its Commander or its AE (Training Officer). A printed copy goes to the Unit Commander; it must be issued the previous day and distributed by 23:00 to external agencies via MIS.
requirements.verbatim: Οι εκπαιδευτικές πτήσεις των Μοιρών εκτελούνται με βάση το Ημερήσιο Πρόγραμμα πτήσεων που εκπονείται από τη Μοίρα και εγκρίνεται από τον Διοικητή ή Α.Ε. αυτής.

requirements.topic: Crew substitutions in the daily programme — Unit Commander briefing/approval; authorization responsibles may fill gaps
requirements.requirement: Limited substitutions of instructors and students are allowed only if they are programmed as reserves in the daily programme, after briefing/approval of the Unit Commander. Those responsible for flight authorization are programmed normally but may cover unforeseen gaps in daily programmes provided preparation/briefing time margins are kept.

requirements.requirement: Student flights may be flown combined with flights of another squadron/MEAE of the same aircraft type, with Unit Commander approval, provided they include maneuvers of the same exercise category.

requirements.topic: Formation leadership — Physical vs Tactical leader; authority limits; tie-break
requirements.requirement: A formation leader is either Physical or Tactical. The leader (either kind) has no disciplinary/command authority over formation members but is authorised to give instructions and orders concerning preparation, planning, execution and debrief of the mission; members must obey regardless of seniority. Physical Leader: the most senior member available on type holding the appropriate lead authorisation; for instructors of different nations, the tie-break is seniority in rank, then higher lead title, and if titles also tie the Physical Lead is DETERMINED by the Commander of the Squadron that orders the flight. Tactical Leader: a flyer authorised to assume lead of the formation/sub-formation for training or tactical purposes, removable at any time at the Physical Leader's discretion.
requirements.verbatim: 18. Ο Αρχηγός ενός Σχηματισμού Α/Φ διακρίνεται σε Φυσικό και σε Τακτικό αρχηγό. requirements.topic: Formation leader — full responsibility catalogue incl. post-flight reporting to command chain
requirements.requirement: The formation leader: reviews members' ground/air performance from their training folders; checks members' psychosomatic fitness, that all members meet prerequisites and are authorised for the specific mission, applicable restrictions, actual/forecast weather on track and alternate, and navaid/frequency/prohibited-area status; conducts the pre-flight briefing per the briefing guide; emphasises and analyses sensitive points; sets technique/tactics so aircraft and member limits are not violated; demands adherence to the briefing and orders deviating members to comply; adheres to mission planning unless safety dictates otherwise; conducts detailed debrief highlighting members' errors; completes grade sheets and checks completion of all books/forms; after debrief informs the Flight Commander, Operations Officer and Squadron Commander of serious member errors and recommends measures; remains the sole direct supervisor in the air.
requirements.verbatim: 21. Ο Αρχηγός του Σχηματισμού ευθύνεται για τα κάτωθι: α. Ενημερώνεται για την απόδοση των μελών του σχηματισμού στο έδαφος και στον αέρα, από τους αντίστοιχους φακέλους εκπσης. β. Ελέγχει: (1) Την κατάλληλη ψυχοσωματική κατάσταση των μελών του σχηματισμού. (2) Αν όλα τα μέλη του σχηματισμού τηρούν τις προϋποθέσεις και είναι εξουσιοδοτημένα για την εκτέλεση της συγκεκριμένης αποστολής. [...] ι. Μετά την απενημέρωση ενημερώνει τον Δκτή Σμήνους, τον Αξκό Επιχειρήσεων και τον Δκτή Μοίρας, για τυχόν σοβαρά σφάλματα μέλους ή μελών του σχηματισμού και εισηγείται τη λήψη μέτρων. ια. Τέλος, έχει πάντα κατά νου ότι στον αέρα είναι ο μοναδικός και άμεσα επιβλέπων και ότι απ' αυτόν εξαρτάται η ασφαλής και επιτυχής εκτέλεση της αποστολής.

requirements.topic: Formation composition minima for scheduling (lead titles required)
requirements.requirement: Minimum lead qualifications of formation members: 2 aircraft — one Pair Leader plus one squadron flyer; 3 aircraft — one Four-ship Leader, one Pair Leader, one squadron flyer; 4 aircraft — one Four-ship Leader, one Pair Leader, two squadron flyers; more than 4 aircraft — one Mission Commander with remaining members as above. A formation may not consist only of attached flyers (exception: Evaluators and T-A Officers of GEA and DAE during evaluations) nor only of flyers under training.

requirements.topic: Formation programming rules — member order, trainee lead as No1, callsigns
requirements.requirement: For drafting flight programmes regarding formations: the order of formation members in the schedule is set by the desired formation position, with the necessary precondition that they hold the formal lead qualifications; in trainee-formation-leader training flights the trainee lead is written as No1 in the formation order with a parallel note in the remarks column; callsigns must correspond to those arising from the printed flight programme to avoid misunderstandings — on ground aborts, the flight supervisors are informed of any changes to the formation numbering set at the pre-flight briefing.

requirements.topic: Mixed aircraft-type formation — Unit Commander approval, VMC only
requirements.requirement: Different aircraft types may fly in formation only after Unit Commander approval, when mission needs permit (SOT, emergency escort etc.), and in VMC only; in IMC such a formation must split.

requirements.topic: Formation Lead — candidate selection criteria and minimum hours
requirements.requirement: Formation-lead candidates must be distinguished (composure, initiative, fighting spirit, professional knowledge, leadership); have grades 8+ in all special characteristics of the last 2 semi-annual characterisation reports with main-mission and instrument grades at least I1; be combat-ready level A (BMC) on the MEA type (otherwise Command informed for exceptional approval). Minimum PIC hours (student-stage hours excluded): Pair Leader 250 hours on MEA type; Four-ship Leader 450 hours (250 on type); Mission Commander 650 hours (250 on type). Past leads regain their title after completing MEAE training, on MEA recommendation.
requirements.verbatim: 5. Η ελάχιστη πτητική εμπειρία ως Κυβερνήτης που πρέπει να διαθέτει ο Ιπτάμενος (Εκπαιδευτής) για Αρχηγός Σχηματισμού είναι: α. requirements.topic: Formation Lead — training and examination procedures per level
requirements.requirement: Pair Leader: Unit order issued 50 hours before hour-completion (training start by Unit order on squadron proposal); ground training of 4 lectures (lead responsibilities, briefing/critique technique, ORM, accidents due to lead error); 6 air sorties SCh-A1 to SCh-A6 mapped to maintenance-stage S-3/S-4 exercises covering BFM, CPM, night; trainee flies as Tactical Leader with the Physical Leader (instructor) being at least a Four-ship Leader senior to him; exam on last flight (SChA-6) by the MEA CO or Training Officer or Unit T-A Officer. Four-ship Leader: no ground training; 3 sorties SChB-1 to SChB-3; Physical Leader at least Mission Commander and senior; exam on SChB-3 by the same officials. Mission Commander: mandatory COMAO seminars at KEAT before hour completion (exempt: Mixed SOT series graduates and past TLP Full Course Participants or equivalent COMAO seminars); no air training or exams — appointed on MEA recommendation if criteria of §§2-6 are met. Evaluation (pair and four-ship): 2 professional questionnaires (50 closed-book + 25 open-book by Unit T-A), 1 GBTS sortie (mission planning, procedures, emergencies, briefing quality), 1 air sortie; evaluated by the Unit T-A Officer or the Unit CO. On completion the Unit issues the Formation Leader Appointment Order, notified to DAE/B6 and GEA/B1.

requirements.topic: Formation Lead — restrictions, deadlines, command-position requirements
requirements.requirement: Lead training/evaluation flown with 2 aircraft (pair) and 3-4 aircraft (four-ship). The candidate must complete training within 3 months after completing required hours. Failure in exam or evaluation triggers the procedures of KPA B-6/GEA and PD 29/2020. Unit COs and Deputy COs, MEA COs and Training Officers MUST hold Mission Commander status — appointed MC without prerequisites as soon as combat-ready on type; Flight Commanders in aircraft squadrons must be Four-ship Leaders and above. Evaluation grade sheet: form A0466; appointment order notified to DAE/B6 and GEA/B1 (AFEI No1 update). In lead-training flights the trainee lead is written as No1 in the formation order with a remarks-column note.

requirements.topic: Squadron Evaluators — who may conduct student evaluations/final exams; appointment; number
requirements.requirement: Evaluations/Final Exams may be flown in all squadrons of the type by: the Squadron CO, the Training/Operations Officer, the squadron Flight Commanders, the Unit T-A Officer, and the Squadron Evaluators. Squadron Evaluators are appointed by the Command (DAE) on Unit recommendation; number fixed at 2 per squadron; for 364MEA one additional Italian Evaluator may be appointed. Prerequisites to be proposed as Squadron Evaluator: hold Instructor Rating category B or above AND be an experienced instructor on type. With Unit CO approval, a squadron's evaluations may be flown by the other squadron's Evaluators. Additionally, if holders of Instructor Rating category B and above, evaluations may be conducted by: the Unit CO, the Deputy CO, the DEE and DPD, and the Evaluators of GEA and DAE.

requirements.topic: Command/GEA Evaluators — special privileges and exclusions
requirements.requirement: To form its view of class performance, the Command evaluates each class before stage end: ground exams for all students plus Air Evaluations by Command (DAE) Evaluators, whose number is set in the Evaluation Order. Command Evaluators may additionally conduct ground or air evaluations and flights at any point of the training flow in every exercise category, including ground exams on professional topics and Bold Face at the end of each stage (on FAIL the exam repeats the next day). Command and GEA Evaluators are NOT counted in the maximum number of instructors per student (Ch.2 §24); squadron Evaluators are not counted in that maximum for Air Evaluations only.

requirements.topic: Evaluation scheduling gates — hours-in-window, no-flight gap, same-day exclusivity
requirements.requirement: Scheduler-enforceable gates for every Evaluation, category Final Exam, Aptitude Exam, Flight-Aptitude-judgment flight or Progress Test: (a) in the last 20 days before any such flight the student must have completed at least 4.0 flight hours regardless of exercise category — if not, he flies REPETITION sorties to complete the hours; (b) if 5 calendar days have passed without flight since the last flight (the day of the last flight excluded), the student is not scheduled for such a flight and flies 1 REPETITION sortie first; (c) a student or trainee scheduled for any Evaluation flight flies NO other sortie the same day (air or F/S), to have adequate preparation time.
requirements.verbatim: ζ. Κάθε μαθητής στις τελευταίες 20 ημέρες πριν από οποιαδήποτε πτήση Αξιολόγησης ή Τελικής Εξέτασης κατηγορίας ασκήσεων, που προβλέπονται από το Αναλυτικό πρόγραμμα του σταδίου ή Εξέταση Καταλληλότητας ή πτήση για κρίση Πτητικής Καταλληλότητας ή Πτήση Δοκιμής Προόδου, πρέπει να έχει συμπληρώσει τουλάχιστον 4,0 ώρες πτήσης ανεξαρτήτως κατηγορίας ασκήσεων. requirements.topic: Student allocation to instructors — command roles excluded, weakest to most experienced
requirements.requirement: For allocating students to instructors (Phases II, III, IV): students performing below class average should go to the most experienced instructors; the Squadron CO and the Training Officer take NO students; effort is made that Flight Commanders take no students — if unavoidable, only one; no student is given to an instructor with any family relation or kinship; foreign students (except Italians) are not given to Italian Air Force instructors unless bilateral agreements provide otherwise.

Να γίνεται προσπάθεια οι μαθητές με απόδοση κάτω του Μ.Ο. του Τμήματος, να δίδονται στους πλέον έμπειρους Εκπαιδευτές. β. requirements.topic: Primary and reserve instructors per student — responsibilities and change rules
requirements.requirement: Each student is assigned one primary and two reserve instructors. The primary instructor is responsible for guidance, progress control and monitoring of the student's Training Folder throughout the stage; reserves assume these duties in order when he is absent; if all three are absent, the respective Flight Commander monitors the training and the student's folder. For ITAF Phase II students at least one instructor must be Italian. Instructor change occurs: (a) in the cases of PD 29/2020 (primary instructor); (b) on posting out or assumption of Flight Commander or Training Officer (AE) duties; (c) by Squadron CO decision for reasons affecting training flow (long absence, long school, long leave). After an instructor change under ANY of these cases, the student no longer flies with the changed instructor for the rest of the stage. The student should also avoid flying with an Evaluator who graded him DEFICIENT or FAIL in an Evaluation flight, unless PD 29/2020 provides otherwise.

requirements.topic: KEPE (Special Monitoring Status of student training) — entry/exit authority and handling duties of Squadron Commander / AE
requirements.requirement: A student enters KEPE at the DISCRETION of the Squadron Commander or its AE when performance lags the training provided, and mandatorily on the listed triggers (single sortie/F-S grade <=59%; two consecutive flights <=63%; two consecutive airsickness flights; FAIL in a written ground exam; FAIL in 2 consecutive/4 non-consecutive oral pre-flight exams; instructor recommendation). Entry/exit is effected by completion of the KEPE Form by the Squadron Commander or the AE, who verify the data, inform the student, coordinate with supporting agencies, set measures (sortie limit to one dual or one F/S per day — a second sortie allowed only if it is a solo; limit number of instructors; extra ground training), set exit goals, monitor daily, and effect exit when weaknesses are eliminated or the stay becomes long without progress.
requirements.verbatim: β. Μαθητής να τίθεται σε ΚΕΠΕ κατά την κρίση του Διοικητή της Μοίρας ή του Α.Ε. αυτής, όταν οι επιδόσεις του στην πτητική ή θεωρητική εκπαίδευση υπολείπονται έναντι της παρεχόμενης εκπαίδευσης... δ. Η είσοδος - έξοδος του μαθητή σε ΚΕΠΕ γίνεται με την συμπλήρωση του αντίστοιχου Φύλλου από τον Διοικητή Μοίρας ή τον Α.Ε. αυτής...
procedure: Verify with squadron instructors the data supporting KEPE entry
Inform the student of his status and the reasons
Cooperate with all agencies supporting training (doctor, instructor, Flight Commander, etc.) to find causes of low performance
Complete the KEPE form with measures: daily sortie limit / instructor-count limit / additional ground training
Record exit goals on the form (codes, general grades, questionnaires, oral exams, solo fitness, any motivating goal at Squadron Commander and AE judgment)
Monitor the student's performance daily and keep training continuous
Effect exit when weaknesses are eliminated and goals achieved, or when the stay becomes long without progress

requirements.topic: Flight Aptitude Board referral — all squadron activities suspended; continuation by order
requirements.requirement: While a student is referred to the Flight Aptitude Board (Symvoulio Ptitikis Ikanotitas) for judgment of flight aptitude (theoretical or flying deficiency), ALL of his squadron activities are interrupted (aircraft flights, F/S flights, ground lessons and exams). The Order continuing the flight training of a student referred to the Board is filed in his Individual Training Folder (AFEI No 2).
requirements.verbatim: Κατά το χρονικό διάστημα παραπομπής του μαθητή στο Συμβούλιο Πτητικής Ικανότητας για κρίση της Πτητικής του Καταλληλότητας (είτε για θεωρητική είτε για Πτητική Ανεπάρκεια), να διακόπτονται όλες οι δραστηριότητές του στη Μοίρα (πτήσεις με Α/Φ, πτήσεις στο F/S, μαθήματα - εξετάσεις εδάφους).
flags: Referral criteria and board procedure are governed by PD 29/2020 (external to the 3-01)

requirements.topic: Phase II oral-exam failure ladder — written exam administered by Squadron Commander or AE
requirements.requirement: Phase II (T-6A): if a student fails 4 consecutive or 8 non-consecutive prescribed oral pre-flight exams, his professional competence is judged by a WRITTEN exam given by the Squadron Commander or the squadron AE, held after 2 calendar days (the failure day excluded), on 50 closed-book + 25 open-book questions + 5 Bold Face/CAPs. On FAIL, re-exam after 2 calendar days on the same items; on a new FAIL, PD 29/2020 applies.
requirements.verbatim: ζ. Όταν αποτυγχάνει σε 4 συνεχόμενες ή 8 μη συνεχόμενες προβλεπόμενες προφορικές εξετάσεις κατά την ομαδική ή/και ατομική προ πτήσεως ενημέρωση, τότε να κρίνεται η επαγγελματική του κατάρτιση με γραπτή εξέταση από τον Δκτή ή τον ΑΕ της Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Substance-influence suspicion — command roles authorized to detect grounds for referral (Phase II)
requirements.requirement: Phase II referral criterion: presenting for flight under the influence of substances is established per the standing directive on addictive/psychotropic substances, upon substantiated indications detected by: the Flight Commander, the Commander or the AE of an Independent Flight/Squadron, the DEE, or the Deputy Commander or the Commander of the Air Force Academy / Group / Wing.
requirements.verbatim: ...κατόπιν βάσιμων ενδείξεων που ανιχνεύονται από τον Διοικητή Σμήνους, τον Διοικητή ή τον ΑΕ Ανεξάρτητου Σμήνους/Μοίρας, τον ΔΕΕ, ή τον Υποδιοικητή ή τον Διοικητή της Σ.Ι./ Σμηναρχίας/Πτέρυγας.

requirements.topic: Student re-currency after abstention — content of unscored flight at Squadron Commander discretion
requirements.requirement: A student with abstention >15 days (pre-solo phase of Phase II/III) or >20 days (rest of the stages) flies, before any scored exercise, 1 unscored flight on maneuvers at the discretion of the Squadron Commander. After >30 days the student loses type currency and follows the re-currency programme of Table 8, whose air sorties repeat taught exercises at the Squadron Commander's discretion (max 1/3 of training received, minimum 1 flight).
requirements.verbatim: ...πριν πετάξει βαθμολογούμενη άσκηση να ίπταται 1 πτήση, χωρίς βαθμολόγηση, σε ελιγμούς κατά την κρίση του Διοικητή της Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Unscored F/S repeat flights — general allowance at Squadron Commander discretion (3 per stage)
requirements.requirement: Each student may fly up to 3 unscored repeat flights in the F/S per training stage, at the discretion of the Squadron Commander.
requirements.verbatim: Κάθε μαθητής δύναται να πετάξει έως 3 πτήσεις επανάληψης στο F/S, ανά Στάδιο εκπαίδευσης, μη βαθμολογούμενες, κατά την κρίση του Δκτή Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Phase II (T-6A) unscored F/S repeat flights — 5 at Squadron Commander discretion
requirements.requirement: In the Basic Stage (Phase II) with T-6A, each student may fly up to 5 unscored F/S REPEAT flights (repeats due to loss of currency not counted), at the discretion of the Squadron Commander.
requirements.verbatim: Κάθε μαθητής δύναται να πετάξει έως 5 πτήσεις ΕΠΑΝΑΛΗΨΗΣ στο F/S, μη βαθμολογούμενες (μη συμπεριλαμβανομένων των πτήσεων ΕΠΑΝΑΛΗΨΗΣ λόγω απώλειας διαθεσιμότητας), κατά την κρίση του Δκτή Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Continuation-stage reduced performance — escalating evaluation ladder through command roles
requirements.requirement: Maintenance stage: after the prescribed additional training, or when an instructor is graded SKE 'A' (in cases not sent directly to aptitude judgment by PD 29/2020), an Air Evaluation is performed by the MEA Commander — or the AE in his absence. If graded 'I3' or 'A' again, an Air Evaluation follows by the Unit T-A Officer or a Command Air Evaluator on the failed exercise; failing to reach SKE 'E','I1' or 'I2' there, the pilot is characterized FAILED and referred for Flight Aptitude judgment (PD 29/2020). The same ladder applies for PR exercises (evaluation by Squadron Commander or AE, then Unit T-A) after up to 25% extra sorties.
requirements.verbatim: ...θα εκτελείται Αξιολόγηση Αέρος από το Δκτή της ΜΕΑ ή τον Α.Ε. σε περίπτωση απουσίας του. Στην περίπτωση που βαθμολογηθεί με «Ι3» ή «Α», θα εκτελείται Αξιολόγηση Αέρος από Αξιωματικό Τ-Α της Μονάδας ή από Αξιολογητή Αέρος της Διοίκησης, στην άσκηση που απέτυχε. Σε περίπτωση που ο εξεταζόμενος δεν επιτύχει ΣΚΕ «Ε», «Ι1» ή «Ι2», θα χαρακτηρίζεται ως ΑΠΟΤΥΧΩΝ και θα τίθεται σε κρίση Πτητικής Καταλληλότητας σύμφωνα με το ΠΔ 29/2020.

requirements.topic: Mission Commander continuation-sortie records — command roles complete the form only on serious observations
requirements.requirement: Flyers holding the Mission Commander title are not required to log their continuation sorties in the Continuation Stage Flight Record form (A0462), EXCEPT when serious observations occurred during the flight, in which case the form is completed by the Flight Commander, the AE, or the MEA/MEAE-SMET Commander.

requirements.topic: Weekly student folder check — signature fallback chain incl. Flight Commander
requirements.requirement: The primary instructor must check the student's Individual Folder at the end of each week and sign the relevant form. In his absence, the Folder is checked and signed by one of the student's reserve instructors, or the Commander of the Flight the student belongs to, or the squadron Standardization Officer.
requirements.verbatim: Σε περίπτωση απουσίας του κύριου Εκπαιδευτή, ο Φάκελος να ελέγχεται και υπογράφεται από έναν εκ των εφεδρικών Εκπαιδευτών του μαθητή ή τον Δκτή Σμήνους στο οποίο ανήκει ή τον Αξιωματικό Τυποποίησης της Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Final Student Performance Report — completed by Flight Commander, endorsed by AE and Squadron Commander
requirements.requirement: The Final Student Performance Report (Teliki Anafora Apodosis Mathiti) is completed by the FLIGHT COMMANDER, and the AE and the SQUADRON COMMANDER give their expert opinions on it, at the end of each training stage of cadets/2Lts. It describes general performance and potential and is filed in the student's AFEI No 2; a copy of the Phase III/IV report goes to GEA/B1.
requirements.verbatim: Συμπληρώνεται από τον Δκτή Σμήνους και γνωματεύουν επ΄ αυτού ο Α.Ε. και Δκτής της Μοίρας (με το τέλος κάθε σταδίου εκπαίδευσης των Ικάρων - Ανθσγών).

requirements.topic: Stage completion report templates — AE writes observations, Squadron Commander gives final characterization, Unit Commander endorses
requirements.requirement: The stage-report templates in the Ch.9 annexes carry dedicated signature blocks: 'OBSERVATIONS of the squadron/MEAE AE' with AE signature, and 'FINAL CHARACTERIZATION of the Squadron/MEAE Commander' with the Squadron Commander's signature; both templates end with an 'ΕΘΕΩΡΗΘΗ / Ο ΔΚΤΗΣ ΜΟΝΑΔΑΣ' block — the Unit Commander endorses these stage reports. requirements.topic: Capacity planning — Squadron Commander and AE excluded from the daily instructor pool but included in instructor strength
requirements.requirement: In the Commencement Report capacity calculation, the daily available instructor force is derived by subtracting from total instructor strength: the Squadron Commander and the AE, plus leave quotas, one instructor at school, two for F/S manning plus MEAE detached, one for PEA/OED manning, and child-care leave. Conversely, the 'Instructor Strength' field of the same report explicitly INCLUDES the Commander and the Operations Officer of the squadron. Instructor daily capacity = 2 sorties per instructor; student capacity factor 0.85 sorties/day pre-solo, 1.2 after.
requirements.verbatim: 1/ Ως δυναμικό Εκπαιδευτών λογίζεται η μέση ημερήσια διαθεσιμότητα Εκπαιδευτών για πτήσεις, που προκύπτει αν από τη συνολική δύναμη αυτών αφαιρεθούν: α/ Ο Διοικητής της Μοίρας και ο Α.Ε. || Συμπεριλαμβάνεται ο Διοικητής και ο Αξιωματικός Επιχειρήσεων της Μοίρας.

requirements.topic: Instructor rating categories Γ/Β/Α — award and extension
requirements.requirement: Instructor Ratings are awarded, promoted or extended by Command order. Category Γ (C): awarded to flyer officers (Greek or foreign) posted for the first time to a training squadron as flight instructors who successfully completed EEP; initial instructional-ability assessment per KPA B-6/GEA by an Air Examiner appointed by Command order. Holders of B or A rating on a different type receive Rating Extension after EEP per KPA B-3/GEA. Foreign-service instructors with a rating from Greece or their posting country receive a rating according to their instructional hours after EEP/re-assignment; without such rating they receive Γ after EEP, later extended per instructional experience gained abroad.

Πτυχίο «Γ» Απονέμεται στους Ιπτάμενους Αξιωματικούς (Έλληνες ή αλλοδαπούς) που τοποθετήθηκαν για πρώτη φορά σε εκπαιδευτική Μοίρα ως Εκπαιδευτές πτήσεων και συμπλήρωσαν επιτυχώς την εκπαίδευσή τους στο στάδιο ΕΕΠ.

requirements.topic: Rating promotion Γ→Β — timing window
requirements.requirement: Promotion from Γ to Β: the exam takes place after completion of 120 hours with student and not beyond 200 hours. If the instructor is not scheduled for the promotion exam after 200 hours with student, the Unit must report the reasons in writing to the Command.
requirements.verbatim: (1) Προαγωγή Πτυχίου από «Γ» σε «Β» Για την Προαγωγή του Πτυχίου πτήσεων από «Γ» σε «Β», η εξέταση να πραγματοποιείται μετά τη συμπλήρωση των 120 ωρών με μαθητή και όχι πάνω από τις 200 ώρες. Σε περίπτωση που ο Εκπαιδευτής δεν προγραμματίζεται για Εξέταση Προαγωγής Πτυχίου μετά τη συμπλήρωση των 200 ωρών με μαθητή, η Μονάδα να αναφέρει εγγράφως στη Διοίκηση τους λόγους μη εκτέλεσης της εξέτασης.

requirements.topic: Rating promotion Β→Α — prerequisites and exam format
requirements.requirement: Promotion from Β to Α requires: 3 years in flight-instructor duties since B award; 300 flight hours since B award; at least 50 classroom teaching hours on aviation subjects, certified in writing by the CO of the Unit where taught (briefing/debriefing hours do not count). Air Examiners for both promotions are appointed by Command order on Unit proposal. The air exam comprises 2 sorties with different Evaluators, grading execution and instruction in representative exercises of the stages where the instructor is employed. The MEA must complete the process within 2 months of Command approval and the Unit report completion within 3 months, otherwise the process restarts. Ground exam: 50-question closed-book and 25-question open-book professional questionnaires.
requirements.verbatim: (α) Να έχει συμπληρώσει 3 έτη στα καθήκοντα του Εκπαιδευτή Πτήσεων από την ημερομηνία που απέκτησε το πτυχίο Εκπαιδευτή κατηγορίας «Β». (β) Να έχει συμπληρώσει 300 ώρες από την ημερομηνία απονομής πτυχίου κατηγορίας «Β». (γ) Να έχει τουλάχιστον 50 ώρες διδασκαλίας στην τάξη σε θέματα αεροπορικού ενδιαφέροντος. [...] (ε) Η Εξέταση στον αέρα περιλαμβάνει 2 εξόδους με διαφορετικούς Αξιολογητές, όπου βαθμολογείται η εκτέλεση και η διδασκαλία σε αντιπροσωπευτικές ασκήσεις των Σταδίων Εκπαίδευσης στα οποία αξιοποιείται ο αξιολογούμενος Εκπαιδευτής.

requirements.topic: Rating exams — success criteria and failure handling
requirements.requirement: Success criterion for Γ award and Γ→Β promotion: final code Ι1 or Ε in the Evaluation flights; failure triggers re-evaluation per KPA B-3/GEA. Success criterion for Β→Α: final code Ε (Excellent) with the restriction that at least 75% of the graded items (EA) are graded '4'; if not achieved in one of the two flights, re-evaluation per Article 13 of KPA B-3/GEA while the instructor retains the B rating in the meantime. Ground-exam rules per KPA B-6/GEA.
requirements.verbatim: (ι) Ως κριτήριο επιτυχίας για την απονομή Πτυχίου «Γ» ή την Προαγωγή Πτυχίου από «Γ» σε «Β», ορίζεται για τις πτήσεις Αξιολόγησης ο τελικός κώδικας «Ι1» ή «Ε». [...] (ια) Ως κριτήριο επιτυχίας για την Προαγωγή Πτυχίου από «Β» σε «Α», ορίζεται για τις πτήσεις Αξιολόγησης ο τελικός κώδικας «Ε» (Εξαίρετος), με τον περιορισμό ότι τουλάχιστον το 75% των ΕΑ στα οποία εξετάσθηκε ο Εκπαιδευτής να έχει βαθμολογηθεί με «4».

requirements.topic: Air Test Pilots — selection criteria, appointment, maximum numbers
requirements.requirement: To be appointed and retain availability as Test Pilot an instructor must: hold Instructor Rating B or above; have 1000 flight hours of which 400 on the squadron's type; be rated 'Very Good' in main mission, instrument flying and flying aptitude in the last 2 semi-annual flyer characterisation reports and 'Excellent' in flight discipline; be distinguished professionally and be available in Adaptation and instrument exercises. Appointment by Unit order on MEA CO proposal, notified to DAE/B6 and GEA/B1. The COs/Training Officers of MEA-MEAE and Unit T-A Officers per type MUST complete the training and be appointed Test Pilots. Maximum 4 Test Pilots per MEA, excluding MEA COs and Training Officers. Additionally, the MEAE CO and Training Officers, the Unit T-A Officers, and attached flyers within the Unit may fly test flights — all three categories provided they were previously characterised Test Pilots on type and retain test-flight availability.
requirements.verbatim: 18. Για να οριστεί, διατεθεί και να διατηρεί τη διαθεσιμότητά του ένας Εκπαιδευτής, ως Δοκιμαστής Α/Φ πρέπει να πληροί τα ακόλουθα κριτήρια: α. Να είναι κάτοχος Πτυχίου Εκπαιδευτή κατηγορίας «Β» και άνω. β. Να έχει πτητική εμπειρία 1000 ωρών εκ των οποίων 400 στον τύπο της Μοίρας. [...] 21. Ως προς τον αριθμό των Δοκιμαστών Αέρος ανά ΜΕΑ, καθορίζεται ότι, αυτός δεν θα ξεπερνά τους 4, μη συμπεριλαμβανομένων των Δκτών και ΑΕ των ΜΕΑ.

requirements.topic: Test Pilot training, evaluation and exclusive privileges
requirements.requirement: Test Pilot training: theory of at least 6 periods by experienced Test Pilots (test-flight analysis, aircraft/system limits, forms, test-area procedures); 2 GBTS sorties with an instructor-test pilot; 1 air sortie (simulated or actual test flight) with an experienced Test Pilot. Evaluation by the Unit T-A Officer or the Squadron CO/Training Officer (if Test Pilot): written 25 open + 25 closed questions per KPA B-6/GEA, 1 GBTS test-simulation sortie, 1 air test-simulation sortie. Privileges: FCF flights are flown only by appointed Test Pilots; Equipment Check Flights may be flown by experienced instructors in maintenance or instructor-training flights (in student flights only with Unit CO approval); taxi tests ONLY by Test Pilots. Test-pilot re-availability: 1 test flight with an available Test Pilot in the rear seat.
requirements.verbatim: 5. Η πτήση παρακολούθησης Α/Φ (Equipment Check Flight), εκτελείται από έμπειρους Εκπαιδευτές πτήσεων σε πτήσεις Συντήρησης ή Εκπαίδευσης Εκπαιδευτών. Δύναται να πραγματοποιείται και σε πτήσεις εκπαίδευσης μαθητών μετά από έγκριση του Δκτή της Μονάδος. 6. Δοκιμή Τροχοδρόμησης θα εκτελείται μόνο από Δοκιμαστές Αέρος.

values.evaluation: 25 open + 25 closed questions, 1 GBTS + 1 air simulation
values.reavailability: 1 test flight with available Test Pilot in rear seat

requirements.topic: FCF seat rules, Test Pilot appointment notification, technician limits, non-certified rear-seat occupants
requirements.requirement: Test flights may be flown with the front seat or both seats occupied; the rear seat is taken by a posted MEA flyer or a technician available for test flights. Test Pilots are appointed by the Unit after training completion, notified to GEA/B1 and DAE/B6. The maximum number of technicians participating in T-6 test flights is 6; the Unit issues the initial-training and appointment order for these technicians on MSA recommendation per MDM 3-24/120PEA. The rear seat of training aircraft may also be occupied by: technicians participating in test flights (also for failure recovery at a remote airfield); flyers of other squadrons/units for exchange of knowledge and experience; other non-certified personnel only on GEA requirement and approval. All such personnel are scheduled for medical-fitness examination by GNA/KAI unless already under its annual medical examination.

requirements.topic: IMC (in-cloud) flight — instructor prerequisites, certification and limits
requirements.requirement: To fly in clouds (with student/trainee or in maintenance) instructors must: have a valid instrument card (P.PDO); be certified for in-cloud flight; and in the last 60 days have flown 1 instrument flight OR 1 night flight OR 3 Special Exercises E-4. requirements.topic: Supervisor of Flying (Epoptis Ptiseon) — role, duties, staffing limits, night restriction

requirements.topic: Demo Pilot — currency, re-qualification and supervision (T-6A)
requirements.requirement: Currency: at least one display flight at 500 ft AGL (high/low/combined, real or practice) every 15 calendar days. Between 15-30 days lapse: either one display at 500 ft with an available Display Instructor, or one at minimum 1000 ft AGL in the presence of the MEA CO with approved stepped descent to 500 ft if no Display Instructor exists. After 30 days: 1 full-profile F/S flight, 1 practice flight starting 5000 ft stepping to 2000 ft then 1000 ft, then 1 display at 500 ft with Display Instructor, or without one — 2 flights at 1000 ft with MEA CO and Ground Safety Observer present, stepping to 500 ft on the 2nd with MEA CO approval. Availability above 1000 ft AGL is lost after 90 days. All solo training display flights are monitored from the ground by the display-instructor acting as Ground Safety Observer; all flights below 2000 ft AGL are video-recorded (archive kept at least 1 year). Grade sheets signed by the MEA CO and the Instructor-Evaluator (initial training) or appointed Demo Safety Observer (maintenance).

requirements.topic: Daily briefings — attendance duty, agenda, exemption cap
requirements.requirement: General squadron briefings are mandatory every day before flying and attended by ALL present flyers of the MEA/MEAE-SMET, following the standardised agenda (weather 5', navigation/NOTAMs 5', Ops Officer or Flight Commander 10' including professional-topics examination, Tactics/Weapons Officer 5' for Phase IV, Standardisation Officer 15' — at least three students/trainees examined on the emergency procedures of the day, Flight Safety Officer 5', lectures up to 10', Squadron CO up to 10'). With squadron programming and Unit Command approval, crews scheduled for it may attend only weather/NOTAMs and proceed to individual briefings (max 30% of the daily programmed flying task, not always the same crews). In the Instructors' Briefing, instructors analyse trainee tendencies and the MEA CO gives directions. In pre-flight individual briefings the instructor examines the student on procedures and asks at least two questions on flight technique, emergency procedures of the day, or flight-related systems.

requirements.requirement: Every maintenance sortie comprises one main exercise (S), enriched with special exercises (E). The Main Exercises S are the basic categories of air exercises, detailed in the Exercise Analyses, to be distributed evenly across the semester: S-1 General Adaptation (retention of handling skills at changing attitudes/AOA/speeds; INCLUDES, for those available, FCF test flights and DEMO flights); S-2 Instrument flying (PDO) day/night (instrument departure, navigation and approach procedures, day or night, VMC or IMC, also ensuring proper preparation before the PDO evaluation per KPA B-6/GEA); S-3 Air-to-Ground missions day/night (approach avoiding A-A and G-A threats to release A-G weapons within TOT window per release criteria); S-4 Air-to-Air missions day/night (detection, interception, surprise, identification and simulated kill by single ship or formation); S-20 No-requirements missions (ferry flights, crew transport, failure-recovery actions etc.). A flight in which less than 75% of the exercise requirements is covered (ADE) is not valid and is logged as S-20.

requirements.topic: Special exercises 'E' — definition, execution and charging rules
requirements.requirement: The Special Exercises E are the quantitative, qualitative and special semi-annual air-exercise requirements each flyer must execute; detailed in the Exercise Analyses; to be distributed evenly over the semester. E items may be executed within ANY main exercise (S) provided aircraft configuration and flying area permit and the restrictions of EE 3-18/DAE are kept. The akin E exercises executable within each S are listed in the S Exercise Analyses' special instructions; if an E is NOT akin to the S flown, the time devoted to it may not exceed 25% of total sortie time. When an E by its nature consumes a large part or the whole sortie, it is charged to the most suitable/nearest akin main exercise (S) as well as to the corresponding E. Executed E exercises are analysed at the pre-flight briefing, logged in the flight log and archived for flying-task control. Covering the minimum E requirements is a parallel responsibility of the flyer himself and the squadron. For any Event with a corresponding PR module, the instructor must have completed that PR training to execute it.

requirements.topic: EVENTS table semantics and landing currencies with automatic renewal chains
requirements.requirement: The EVENTS table (Ch.4 §48) shows per event: which Events must be PROGRAMMED; which are required for BMC or AMC combat-ready characterization; the AVAILABILITY duration in days, split for inexperienced (AP) and experienced (EMP) flyers — where no number is printed the flyer retains availability forever; which aircraft can execute each Event (capability does not imply obligation); which Events allow re-availability/renewal in the FMS; which allow renewal via the 2nd type for dual-type flyers; and from which pilot seat each Event may be executed. Landing currencies: DAY LANDING (Π/Γ ημέρας) — required for BMC and AMC, validity 90 days (single figure spanning the AP/EMP columns), both types, both seats. NIGHT LANDING (Π/Γ νύκτας) — required for AMC, validity 45 days (inexperienced) / 60 days (experienced), both types, both seats. Renewal chains: a night landing automatically renews the day landing; a landing from the rear seat automatically renews the front-seat landing.

requirements.topic: Loss of type availability and re-assignment tiers (maintenance-stage instructors)
requirements.requirement: An instructor in the maintenance phase loses type availability after abstention from flying of more than 180 days (inexperienced) or more than 1 year (experienced). Re-assignment training is provided at the MEAE/SMET, scaled by experience and length of abstention. Experienced, 1-2 years: abbreviated systems course at MEAE/SET; GBTS normal/emergency procedure checks; 50-question closed-book systems exam; at least 15% of the MET+EEP air programme — the BASE percentage set at the discretion of the MEAE Commander per abstention and experience; at least 25% of the GBTS programme. Experienced, over 2 years: abbreviated course; GBTS checks; 50-question systems + 50-question professional + 25-question open-book exams; at least 15% of the air programme increased by 5% per extra year of abstention beyond 2 years up to 30% — the escalation and its cap at the discretion of the UNIT; 50% of the GBTS programme. Inexperienced, 180 days-1 year: as experienced 1-2y items (a)-(c) plus at least 15% air (MEAE CO discretion) and at least 25% GBTS. Inexperienced, over 1 year: abbreviated course; F/S or GBTS procedure checks plus 100-question closed-book systems exam; 20% of the air programme increased by at least 10% per year of abstention beyond one year up to 50%, at the discretion of the Unit; 50% of the GBTS programme. Exceptionally, for rating-A holders posted to positions of responsibility the MET/EEP programme may be reduced further on Unit recommendation. After completion the MEA submits a Re-assignment Completion Report and requests approval to employ the re-assigned flyer; the report also goes to DAE when a rating extension is involved.

requirements.topic: Advanced (PR) exercises — framework: gates, deadlines, instructors, certification, restoration
requirements.requirement: Advanced Exercises (PR) are certain main and special operational exercises with execution particularities; initial assignment requires training per sortie, after which flyers retain availability per the semi-annual programmes. Training in PR may begin only after the instructor completes 10 sorties following posting to the squadron (except PR requiring a formation-lead title). Ground training precedes flying and includes theory plus one F/S sortie per module. The overall PR programme completes within 7 months of start (except PR requiring a formation-lead title); in distinct PR modules each sortie must be at most 10 calendar days after the previous (e.g. PR-1b after PR-1a), else the previous sortie is repeated. Instructors used for PR training must be at least Four-ship Leaders and available in the exercises. In the last sortie of each module, certification for the specific PR is performed and recorded in the grade sheet; the certification flight is flown by the Flight Commander, Training Officer, Squadron CO, or Unit T-A Officer. Flyers previously assigned to such exercises as PIC on a fighter, or with up to 2 years abstention from them on the same type, may follow a reduced programme at squadron discretion, not below 1/3 of the total programme pro rata, prioritising the co-pilot sorties. If crews have LOST availability in these exercises, the initial re-assignment method is determined on Unit proposal with Command approval.
